dimensions.gloss: Which AI tool, system, or provider was used, including its name, version, and (for translation-specific cases) tool selection.
variants: the selection and use of translation tools
what ai tool(s) have you used?
dimensions.note: Includes both specific tool naming and broader tool-type/category classifications (e.g. LLM vs. AI-assisted tool); 'version and date of use' also carries an access-date component but is primarily about system version.

dimensions.canonical_label: Extent/tier of AI use governing disclosure
dimensions.gloss: How much or what kind of AI contribution is permitted or triggers a disclosure obligation, expressed as scopes, thresholds, tiers, or lanes.
variants: the scope of permissible ai use

dimensions.gloss: Whether and how AI-produced content or claims were checked, confirmed, or graded for correctness before being accepted.
variants: what made you decide to accept, modify or reject ai's suggestions?
dimensions.note: 'traffic-light certification' is a graded review-outcome scheme (auto-certify/human review/reject) rather than an extent-of-use tier, so it was placed here rather than with extent-of-ai-use.

dimensions.canonical_label: Type of role or task contributed
dimensions.gloss: What specific task, role, or labor category a human or AI contributor performed (CRediT-like taxonomies of authorship/contribution work).
variants: two new credit taxa and revisions to three existing taxa
whether guidance was generated or adapted by ai
dimensions.note: 'whether guidance was generated or adapted by ai' is a close call: it could be read as an extent-of-use question, but the quote frames it as classifying what the AI did (generate vs. adapt), matching this axis better.

dimensions.gloss: Where in a document or manuscript an AI-use disclosure must or does appear (e.g. methods, acknowledgements, cover letter, a named section).
variants: use of ai must be declared in the cover letter
use of ai must be declared in the main manuscript
whether and how ai applications were used
dimensions.note: 'title & abstract' is a close call: it is a manuscript-section marker from a reporting checklist rather than an AI-disclosure-specific field, but it shares the same underlying axis of where in a document something must be stated.

dimensions.gloss: Transparency invoked as a broad normative value or requirement (disclose AI use, provide detail, be open) rather than as a specific measurable field.
variants: transparent disclosure of artificial intelligence use
dimensions.note: Deliberately kept apart from disclosure-location-placement per the instruction that vague-virtue transparency and named-field transparency are different axes; 'transparency across the ai lifecycle' is a close call since it is a named checklist domain, not merely a slogan.

dimensions.gloss: Whether a disclosure signals that a human remains in charge of, explains, or takes responsibility for AI-assisted output.
variants: whether the cue communicated human oversight or editorial accountability

dimensions.gloss: Where content, data, or output originated and how it was transformed along the way, including synthetic-data flags, watermark traces, and which inputs shaped it.
variants: which parts of the data are synthetic

dimensions.gloss: Whether the data, software, or tool used carries a stable identifier or resolvable link for citation.
variants: url/link to the data/software, preferably persistent identifier (e.g., doi) and resolves

dimensions.gloss: Whether and how datasets, software, or models are version-controlled and versioned over time as a citation/documentation practice.
dimensions.note: Distinguished from tool-identity, which is about which tool/version was used for a task, whereas this cluster is about the general practice of tracking artifact versions for citation.

dimensions.gloss: How much transformative or creative input a human contributed to AI-assisted output, relevant to authorship/ownership determinations.
The function or format of a reference to software in text (e.g. informal mention vs. formal citation, allusion vs. usage vs. creation).

dimensions.canonical_label: Stage/phase of use in the workflow
dimensions.gloss: At which point or phase of a task or process the AI was engaged (e.g. outlining, translation, editing; data processing vs. drafting).
dimensions.note: 'tri-layer interaction model' is a close call: it is an Ask-Plan-Craft interaction model for a countermeasure design rather than a disclosure field, but it structurally names the same kind of phase/stage axis.

dimensions.gloss: Which functional use case or risk category an AI application falls into, used to determine what disclosure treatment applies.
dimensions.note: 'vulnerability zones' is a close call: it classifies risk by task context in an academic-integrity setting rather than by product use case, but shares the same risk-tiering-by-context logic.

dimensions.gloss: Where an AI artifact or claim is valid, where it fails, and what a documentary record can and cannot settle.
dimensions.note: 'two classes' (what a record can vs. cannot settle) is a close call, grouped here as an epistemic-limits statement rather than with verification-of-output.

dimensions.gloss: Whether a statement, claim, or control is traceable to evidence or a supporting protocol, and whether reasoning can itself be checked.
variants: what evidence or protocol supports it

dimensions.gloss: What the AI actually produced or returned as output, as distinct from the tool used or the task purpose.
Why AI was used for a given task, i.e. the stated purpose or reasoning behind the decision to employ it.
variants: their reasoning behind their decision to employ ai

dimensions.gloss: Whether and how a system or disclosure communicates what remains unknown or uncertain about AI output.
A specific named editing/refining pass in an AI-assisted writing workflow, each tied to a characteristic risk.
A scheme's own umbrella heading introducing a bespoke list of themes or topic areas, without itself naming one specific disclosure axis.
dimensions.note: Catch-all for heading-type labels that name a set of study-specific themes rather than a single axis; kept distinct from the four 'theme: X' labels below, which each name a specific axis of an incident-disclosure record.

dimensions.gloss: Whether a promotional giveaway mechanism is present in the content being coded.
A survey section heading covering disclosure about the research team itself, as one of several study themes.
dimensions.note: Uncertain fit: this reads as a section label of a survey instrument rather than a measurable disclosure axis in its own right.

dimensions.gloss: How detailed or strict a disclosure requirement is, ranging from vague to highly specific.
Whether the endorser's stated or implied attitude toward the promoted product is positive or negative.
variants: the youtuber’s valence regarding the product

dimensions.gloss: What caused an AI-related incident, as a coded facet of an incident-disclosure record.
The harm, risk, or downstream action an AI-related incident caused, as a coded facet of an incident-disclosure record.
Which party is identified as responsible for an AI-related incident.
Which party first revealed or disclosed an AI-related incident to the public.
Whether a deliverable can be used, maintained, and handed off by a competent third party without privileged creator knowledge.
A construct measuring the ratio between who is credited as a thought leader and who performed the actual (possibly hidden) labor.
A grouping of influencer misconduct types (e.g. misinformation, offensive language, privacy violations) relevant to disclosure ethics.
A latent profile or configuration describing a distinct pattern of how users engage with AI tools.
The distinct parties (e.g. instructors, students, control authorities) a policy framework is structured around.

dimensions.canonical_label: Process for developing a role taxonomy
dimensions.gloss: The procedural steps by which a scheme decides which contributor roles to add, exclude, or integrate into its standard list.
A named framework of distinct gaps (attribution, source, response) in the ability to verify journalistic claims.
dimensions.note: Close call against verification-validation-of-ai-output: kept separate because it names types of unverifiability rather than a verification method actually applied.

dimensions.gloss: A fixed compact logging format combining which artifact was adopted, its role label, and the human judgment applied.
Whether and how AI tools are reviewed or approved before being permitted for use.
Trustworthiness named as the overarching meta-principle governing a media organization's conduct.
A framework distinguishing a confidentiality threshold (protecting entrusted material) from a judgment threshold (protecting human responsibility for reasoning).
A composite coding category for whether an alcohol brand is visible, whether disclosure is present, and whether a slogan accompanies it.
Whether promotional content uses an emotional or rational persuasive appeal.
How openly and under what conditions a person discloses AI use, ranging from avoidance to proactive full transparency.
A classification of advertising content by its label, media format, and how organic and sponsored elements are mixed.
Categories of human labor value at stake when AI use is disclosed or hidden (e.g. relational presence, aesthetic provenance, accountability).
A categorization of how AI replaces or substitutes for a human task or role.
dimensions.note: Kept as its own singleton: the source quote gives no substantive content to confirm which specific axis this measures.

dimensions.gloss: A classification of which kinds of artifact count as software (e.g. application, plugin, operating system, programming environment).

dimensions.canonical_label: Types of AI-generated content by posting context
dimensions.gloss: A classification of AI-generated content by who posted it and its relationship to the platform (user-posted, integrated tool, platform-posted).
A classification of distributors into active and passive types.
A table column giving typical concrete examples of a category, rather than naming a disclosure axis itself.
dimensions.note: This is a formatting/illustration artifact rather than a substantive axis, but every label must land somewhere.

dimensions.gloss: The dimensions (trustworthiness, expertise, aesthetics) along which a source or influencer's credibility is assessed.
The degree of model uncertainty, weak provenance, or disagreement with human assessment used to decide whether to escalate.
Who holds ultimate authority over whether an AI agent entity persists over time.
dimensions.note: The label name suggests a data-citation principle, but the example quote is about human-operator authority over an agent's continued existence, so it was kept separate from persistent-identifier/artifact-versioning.

dimensions.gloss: The hierarchical level (national, university, course) at which AI-use policy is set.
Whether AI use must be disclosed at all, as a yes/no/unsure requirement, independent of where or how.
variants: use of ai must be disclosed in some form

dimensions.gloss: A broad set of named ethical values (privacy, trust, safety, responsibility, explainability, etc.) a scheme organizes itself around.
A named principle requiring generative AI output to fully adopt the presentation style of genuine journalistic articles.
Whether text reveals whose stance or voice the words index (none/potential/clear).
Whether text signals that the worker is uncertain (none/potential/clear).
The dominant stylistic way commercial or promotional content is presented (e.g. playful portrait, tutorial, product test, lifestyle).
The criteria audiences use to judge journalistic content as authentic (fact-based, source-identifiable, human-written, etc.).
variants: what do you consider authentic journalistic content?

dimensions.gloss: What prompts or input a person drafted when using an AI tool.
variants: what prompts did you draft when using ai?

dimensions.gloss: The rules that determine when an AI-assisted process should stop or be escalated.

dimensions.canonical_label: Whether AI can be a coauthor
dimensions.gloss: Whether an AI tool can be considered a coauthor of a work, as opposed to merely an assisting tool.
variants: whether ai tools can be considered as coauthors

dimensions.gloss: Whether a professional or expert human review option is available as a safeguard on AI output.
dimensions.note: Close call against verification-validation-of-ai-output: kept separate because this is about the availability of a review option rather than verification actually performed.

dimensions.gloss: Which specific controls or safeguards an organization states that it operates.
The specific phrase or label chosen to describe AI involvement (e.g. "AI-generated" vs. "AI-assisted").

dimensions.canonical_label: Workflow exposure of AI output to users
dimensions.gloss: Whether, when, where, to whom, and in what form AI output was presented within an operational system's user interface.
The publication year recorded as a citation/reference metadata field.
The distinct loci (faculty intention, formal policy, student interpretation, student self-policy, student practice) at which an AI-use policy is defined or enacted along an implementation chain.
